s.t:
The Intermittent Staff Physician - Neurology will provide direct and supervisory neurological medical care to veterans and /or employees at inpatient/outpatient sites selected as appropriate. The staff physician will also teach neurology residents and students clinical neurosciences.

Scope of Assigned Duties Functions within scope of a staff physician - neurologist as defined Makes assessments of individual and group needs and provides appropriate changes to educational paradigm.

Works with clinical staff on observing veteran's response to modifies treatment plan as appropriate with the needs of veterans, including transfer to other levels of class as appropriate Collaborates effectively with members of the interdisciplinary team to ensure the continuation of quality health care.

VA offers a comprehensive total rewards package. VHA Physician Total Rewards. Pay: Competitive salary, annual performance bonus, regular salary increases. Licensure: 1 full and unrestricted license from any US State or territory. Malpractice: Free liability protection with tail coverage provided.

Contract: No Physician Employment Contract and no significant restriction on moonlighting. Work Schedule: This position has no set tour hours; work is scheduled based on clinical demand and the employee is compensated only for hours actually worked.
To qualify for this position, you must meet the basic requirements as well as any additional requirements (if applicable) listed in the job announcement. Applicants pending the completion of training or license requirements may be referred and tentatively selected but may not be hired until all requirements are met.

Currently employed physician(s) in VA who met the requirements for appointment under the previous qualification standard at the time of their initial appointment are deemed to have met the basic requirements of the occupation.

Basic Requirements: United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy. Degree of doctor of medicine or an equivalent degree resulting from a course of education in allopathic medicine or osteopathic medicine.

The degree must have been obtained from one of the schools approved by the Department of Veterans Affairs for the year in which the course of study was completed. Current, full and unrestricted license to practice medicine or surgery in a State, Territory, or Commonwealth of the United States, or in the District of Columbia.

Residency Training: Physicians must have completed residency training, approved by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs in an accredited core specialty training program leading to eligibility for board certification.

(NOTE: VA physicians involved in academic training programs may be required to be board certified for faculty status.) Approved residencies are: (1) Those approved by the accrediting bodies for graduate medical education, the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) or American Osteopathic Association (AOA), in the list published for the year the residency, or fellowship if applicable, was completed; OR (2) One year of post medical school training (internship, first year of residency, or transitional year residency) approved by ACGME or AOA followed by two years of post-training independent practice (performing under a full and unrestricted license) in the United States; OR (3) Non-US residency training programs followed by a minimum of three years of verified independent practice in the United States (performing under a full and unrestricted license) performing duties related to the position they are applying for (United States fellowships would be creditable towards this requirement), which the local Medical Staff Executive Committee deems to have provided the applicant with appropriate professional training and believes has exposed the Physician to an appropriate range of patient care experiences.

Exceptions: Residents currently enrolled in ACGME/AOA accredited residency training programs and who would otherwise meet the basic requirements for appointment are eligible to be appointed as "Physician Resident Providers" (PRPs).

PRPs must be fully licensed physicians (i.e., not a training license) and may only be appointed on an intermittent basis. PRPs are not considered independent practitioners and will not be privileged; rather, they are to have a "scope of practice" that allows them to perform certain restricted duties under supervision.

Additionally, surgery residents in gap years may also be appointed as PRPs.

In rare and unusual circumstances, the Facility Director can submit a memo to the VISN Director through the VISN Chief Medical Officer, who may approve requests for reasonable exceptions to the residency training requirement for Physicians whose composite record of experience, accomplishments, performance, and qualifications warrant such action.

Proficiency in spoken and written English. Board Certification.

Physicians are generally not required to be board certified for employment in VA; however, three circumstances in VA require Physician board certification: If the position being filled is required to be a supervisor for medical students or Physician residents (including fellows), the LCME, ACGME, or AOA standards requiring a particular board certification credential will apply.

If the position being filled will have faculty status with an affiliated medical school (for example, in joint recruitments with affiliated medical schools), then a medical school requirement for board certification will apply to the jointly recruited position.

If the position being filled is required to be board certified by virtue of specific VHA policy (for example, as director of a cardiac catheterization laboratory or Director of Clinical Laboratory Medicine), then VHA policy requiring board certification will apply.

Preferred Experience: Fellowship training in demyelinating disease, headaches, neuromuscular disease and movement disorders preferred. Reference: For more information on this qualification standard, please visit https://www.va.gov/ohrm/QualificationStandards/. Physical Requirements: VA Handbook 5019

To qualify for this position, you must meet the basic requirements as well as any additional requirements (if applicable) listed in the job announcement. Applicants pending the completion of training or license requirements may be referred and tentatively selected but may not be hired until all requirements are met.

Currently employed physician(s) in VA who met the requirements for appointment under the previous qualification standard at the time of their initial appointment are deemed to have met the basic requirements of the occupation.

Basic Requirements: United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy. Degree of doctor of medicine or an equivalent degree resulting from a course of education in allopathic medicine or osteopathic medicine.

The degree must have been obtained from one of the schools approved by the Department of Veterans Affairs for the year in which the course of study was completed. Current, full and unrestricted license to practice medicine or surgery in a State, Territory, or Commonwealth of the United States, or in the District of Columbia.

Residency Training: Physicians must have completed residency training, approved by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs in an accredited core specialty training program leading to eligibility for board certification.

(NOTE: VA physicians involved in academic training programs may be required to be board certified for faculty status.) Approved residencies are: (1) Those approved by the accrediting bodies for graduate medical education, the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) or American Osteopathic Association (AOA), in the list published for the year the residency, or fellowship if applicable, was completed; OR (2) One year of post medical school training (internship, first year of residency, or transitional year residency) approved by ACGME or AOA followed by two years of post-training independent practice (performing under a full and unrestricted license) in the United States; OR (3) Non-US residency training programs followed by a minimum of three years of verified independent practice in the United States (performing under a full and unrestricted license) performing duties related to the position they are applying for (United States fellowships would be creditable towards this requirement), which the local Medical Staff Executive Committee deems to have provided the applicant with appropriate professional training and believes has exposed the Physician to an appropriate range of patient care experiences.

Exceptions: Residents currently enrolled in ACGME/AOA accredited residency training programs and who would otherwise meet the basic requirements for appointment are eligible to be appointed as "Physician Resident Providers" (PRPs).

PRPs must be fully licensed physicians (i.e., not a training license) and may only be appointed on an intermittent basis. PRPs are not considered independent practitioners and will not be privileged; rather, they are to have a "scope of practice" that allows them to perform certain restricted duties under supervision.

Additionally, surgery residents in gap years may also be appointed as PRPs.

In rare and unusual circumstances, the Facility Director can submit a memo to the VISN Director through the VISN Chief Medical Officer, who may approve requests for reasonable exceptions to the residency training requirement for Physicians whose composite record of experience, accomplishments, performance, and qualifications warrant such action.

* Sie schätzen die interdisziplinäre Zusammenarbeit und bringen sich gerne aktiv ins Team ein
* Sie sind zuverlässig, flexibel und teamorientiert
* Sie möchten nicht nur behandeln, sondern auch mitgestalten und Teil der lups sein - beispielsweise bei Konzepten, Projekten und der Weiterentwicklung unserer Angebote

* Ein wertschätzendes, unterstützendes Arbeitsklima, indem Zusammenarbeit gelebt wird

* Familienfreundliche Anstellungsbedingungen, die Beruf und Privatleben gut miteinander vereinbaren lassen
* Attraktive langfristige Entwicklungs- und Gestaltungsmöglichkeiten
## Besonderes ##
* Interne und externe Supervisionen sowie individuell abgestimmte Weiterbildungen

* Viel Raum für Eigeninitiative, fachliche Entfaltung und persönliche Schwerpunkte.

Die Luzerner Psychiatrie AG ist Lehrspital der Universität Luzern und mit Ihren Angeboten an verschiedenen Standorten im Kanton Luzern und in Sarnen, Kanton Obwalden vertreten. **Zur Verstärkung unseres Teams suchen wir per 1. November 2026 oder nach Vereinbarung eine engagierte Persönlichkeit als Oberärztin / Oberarzt Orthopädie/ Traumatologie & Sportmedizin, die Verantwortung übernimmt und unsere Klinik in Zukunft aktiv mitgestalten möchte.**
Am Spital Thun erwartet Sie das gesamte Spektrum der Orthopädie/Traumatologie und Sportmedizin. Ihr Aufgabenbereich umfasst sowohl die operative Versorgung der Patient:innen (bei Bedarf mit Unterstützung durch die Leitenden Ärzt:innen) als auch die Abdeckung der Sprechstunde und der Pikettdienste.
Sie übernehmen eigenverantwortlich und mit eigenständigen Handlungsspielraum die Betreuung von Patient:innen mit Verletzungen und Erkrankungen des gesamten Bewegungsapparates. Sie beteiligen sich aktiv an internen- und externen Weiterbildungsveranstaltungen.
## Das wartet auf Sie ##
* Anerkannte Weiterbildungsstätte für den interdisziplinären Schwerpunkt Orthopädie/Traumatologie und Sportmedizin
* Ein breites operatives und konservatives Behandlungsspektrum mit hoher Eigenverantwortung in einer Klinik der Kategorie B1
* Attraktive Möglichkeiten zur fachlichen und persönlichen Weiterentwicklung - inklusive Unterstützung von Kursen, Kongressen und Fortbildungen
* Regelmässige klinikinterne Fortbildungen
* Sie werden Teil eines motivierten, kollegialen Teams mit wertschätzender Zusammenarbeit
* Kurze Entscheidungswege und eine offene, wertschätzende Teamkultur mit flacher Hierarchie
* Supervision und Weiterbildung unserer Assistenzärztinnen und Assistenzärzte
* Flexible Arbeitsmodelle, attraktive Anstellungsbedingungen mit der Option auf zusätzliche Ferientage
* Schöner Arbeitsplatz im Berner Oberland mit hoher Lebensqualität
Ihre Aufgaben
* Selbstständige Betreuung von ambulanten und stationären Patient:innen
* Operative Tätigkeit im Bereich Orthopädie und Traumatologie entsprechend Ihrer Erfahrung und Spezialisierung
* Mitwirkung im traumatologischen Dienst sowie in der Versorgung von Notfallpatient:innen
## So werden Sie Teil unseres Teams ##
* Facharzttitel Orthopädische Chirurgie/Traumatologie FMH oder äquivalent (oder kurz vor Abschluss der Ausbildung)
* Eine teamorientierte Persönlichkeit mit ausgeprägter Kommunikations- und Kooperationsfähigkeit für eine gute interdisziplinäre und interprofessionelle Zusammenarbeit
* Hohe Sozialkompetenz, Belastbarkeit, Eigeninitiative und Verantwortungsbewusstsein mit grossem Interesse an der Traumatologie

Die Universitätsklinik für Dermatologie des Inselspitals Bern gehört zu den renommiertesten Hautkliniken der Schweiz.

Die Dermatopathologie nimmt darin eine Schlüsselrolle ein: Als Bindeglied zwischen klinischer Diagnostik, Therapie, Lehre und Forschung erbringt unser akkreditiertes Labor jährlich mehr als 20'000 Befundungen an Hautpräparaten -- von Routineuntersuchungen über immunhistochemische Analysen bis hin zu komplexer molekularpathologischer Diagnostik in enger Zusammenarbeit mit dem Clinical Genomics Laboratory des Inselspitals.

Das Labor ist zudem als ICDP-Trainingszentrum anerkannt und versteht die Förderung des ärztlichen Nachwuchses als selbstverständliche Aufgabe. Für die Leitung dieser Einheit suchen wir eine diagnostisch versierte, wissenschaftlich engagierte Persönlichkeit mit Freude an Gestaltung.
**Das erwartet Sie**
* Gesamtleitung der Abteilung Dermatopathologie in fachlicher, personeller und betriebswirtschaftlicher Hinsicht.
* Personalführung eines multiprofessionellen Teams: Dermatopatholog:innen, Labormitarbeiter:innen (BMA, Laborassistenz) und ADministration -- inkl. Mitarbeitendengespräche, Entwicklungsplanung und Rekrutierung.
* Budget- und Ressourcenverantwortung: Kostenstellenführung, Wirtschaftlichkeitskontrolle, Investitionsplanung und Mitarbeit bei der Leistungsverrechnung.
* Eigenverantwortliche Befundung im gesamten Spektrum der dermatologischen Histopathologie -- inkl. immunhistochemischer und molekularpathologischer Diagnostik.
* Regelmässige Präsentation histologischer Befunde in klinisch-pathologischen Konferenzen sowie im interdisziplinären Hauttumorboard.
* Treiber:in der digitalen Transformation: Einführung und Weiterentwicklung digitaler Pathologie-Workflows (Whole Slide Imaging, KI-gestützte Diagnostikunterstützung), LIS-Optimierung und Schnittstellengestaltung zu klinischen Informationssystemen.
* Strategische Weiterentwicklung des Labors: Einführung neuer Methoden, Prozessoptimierung, Sicherstellung der ICDP-Akkreditierung.
* Enge Zusammenarbeit mit der dermatologischen Poliklinik und dem Clinical Genomics Laboratory der Universität Bern
* Verantwortung für Lehre, Weiterbildung und Betreuung von Assistenzärzt:innen sowie Studierenden im Bereich der Dermatopathologie
* Initiierung, Leitung und Förderung von Forschungsprojekten mit Einbezug der Dermatopathologie
**Das bringen Sie mit**
* Facharzttitel FMH für Dermatologie und Venerologie mit Schwerpunkt Dermatopathologie
* ICDP-Diplom (International Board Certification in Dermatopathology) erworben
* Mehrjährige Erfahrung in der eigenverantwortlichen histopathologischen Diagnostik; erste Führungserfahrung in einer leitenden Funktion von Vorteil.
* Bereitschaft zur Übernahme von Personalverantwortung für ein interdisziplinäres Team aus Ärzteschaft, BMA und Laborassistenz.
* Betriebswirtschaftliches Grundverständnis: Erfahrung mit Budgetverantwortung, Leistungssteuerung und Ressourcenplanung.
* Affinität zur Digitalisierung: Erfahrung mit digitaler Pathologie, LIS-Systemen oder KI-gestützten Anwendungen
* Interesse an der Weiterentwicklung diagnostischer Methoden und an der Schnittstelle zur molekularen Pathologie.
* Wissenschaftliche Neugier und nachweisliche eigene Forschungstätigkeit oder klarer akademischer Entwicklungsplan.
* Freude an der Ausbildung und Förderung von Assistenzärzt:innen
* Stilsicheres Deutsch und Englisch in Wort und Schrift; Kenntnisse des Französischen sind willkommen.
* Analytische Präzision, Eigenverantwortung und ein verbindliches, kollegiales Auftreten.
**Unser Angebot**
* Leitungsfunktion mit Gestaltungsspielraum: Sie prägen die Ausrichtung, das Team und die Prozesse der Abteilung aktiv mit.
* Digitalisierung: Möglichkeit, mit Einführung digitaler Pathologie Massstäbe zu setzen
* Einzigartiges Fallspektrum: um 20'000 Präparate jährlich, darunter viele seltene und komplexe Fälle
* Etabliertes Labor für interne und externe Einsender und eingespieltes Team von xxx Laboranten
* Akademische Perspektive: eigene Forschungslinien, internationale Vernetzung
* ICDP-Trainingszentrum: Sie formen den dermatopathologischen Nachwuchs der Schweiz aktiv mit.
* Attraktive Anstellungsbedingungen (Personalrestaurant, familienfreundliche Arbeitszeitmodelle, Weiterbildungszeit).
* Standort Bern: hohe Lebensqualität, exzellente Verkehrsanbindung, internationales Umfeld.

Basic Requirements: United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy. Approved residencies are: (1) Those approved by the accrediting bodies for graduate medical education, the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) or American Osteopathic Association (AOA), in the list published for the year the residency, or fellowship if applicable, was completed; OR (2) One year of post medical school training (internship, first year of residency, or transitional year residency) approved by ACGME or AOA followed by two years of post-training independent practice (performing under a full and unrestricted license) in the United States; OR (3) Non-US residency training programs followed by a minimum of three years of verified independent practice in the United States (performing under a full and unrestricted license) performing duties related to the position they are applying for (United States fellowships would be creditable towards this requirement), which the local Medical Staff Executive Committee deems to have provided the applicant with appropriate professional training and believes has exposed the Physician to an appropriate range of patient care experiences.

Exceptions: Residents currently enrolled in ACGME/AOA accredited residency training programs and who would otherwise meet the basic requirements for appointment are eligible to be appointed as "Physician Resident Providers" (PRPs).

PRPs must be fully licensed physicians (i.e., not a training license) and may only be appointed on an intermittent basis. PRPs are not considered independent practitioners and will not be privileged; rather, they are to have a "scope of practice" that allows them to perform certain restricted duties under supervision.

Additionally, surgery residents in gap years may also be appointed as PRPs.

réso.ne est le nouveau réseau de santé ambulatoire de référence du canton de Neuchâtel.
Né de la volonté du Réseau hospitalier neuchâtelois (RHNe) de renforcer durablement l'offre de soins de proximité, réso.ne s'inscrit au cœur de la politique sanitaire cantonale 2025-2030. Sa mission est de garantir à la population un accès coordonné, performant et pérenne aux soins ambulatoires, en complémentarité étroite avec la médecine de ville et l'ensemble des acteurs du système de santé.
réso.ne développe un réseau intégré de centres médicaux répartis sur le territoire cantonal, notamment à Neuchâtel, La Chaux-de-Fonds, Fleurier et Geneveys-sur-Coffrane. Cette organisation favorise la continuité des soins, la coordination entre les professionnels et une prise en charge fluide des patients, qu'il s'agisse de consultations programmées, de suivi longitudinal ou de situations urgentes non vitales.
Grâce à un partenariat fort avec le RHNe, réso.ne bénéficie d'un accès privilégié aux expertises hospitalières, aux projets médicaux innovants, à des outils de coordination modernes et l-accès facilité à la formation continue et à la documentation. Cette collaboration permet de renforcer les liens entre les acteurs, et à améliorer le parcours de soins des patients.
Au-delà de sa mission clinique, réso.ne place la formation et la transmission des savoirs au cœur de son développement. Rejoindre réso.ne, c'est participer à un projet de santé ambitieux et innovant, porté par des valeurs de proximité, de collaboration et d'excellence. Le Département de médecine de premier recours (DMPR) a pour mission sociétale de permettre un accès aux soins de qualité pour tous par une médecine de proximité, d-assurer la prise en charge des urgences médicales et chirurgicales légères, de promouvoir la prévention auprès des citoyennes et citoyens, d-apporter les connaissances médicales aux investigations judiciaires et de promouvoir la santé des voyageurs et voyageuses.
De par la polyvalence de ses compétences, le Centre universitaire romand de médecine légale (CURML) a pour mission de répondre à toutes les demandes d-expertises ou d-assistance-conseil dans le domaine médico-légal, du droit médical et de l-analyse du dopage. Situé au niveau de l-arc lémanique, son domaine de compétences s-exerce tant au niveau régional, national qu-international.
L-Unité de Médecine et Psychologie du Trafic (UMPT) du CURML effectue des expertises médicales d-aptitude à la conduite, des expertises psychologiques d-aptitude à la conduite, des expertises médico-psychologiques d-aptitude à la conduite.

L-UMPT dispose de deux médecins de niveau 4, spécialistes en médecine du trafic SSML et deux psychologues spécialistes en psychologie de la circulation FSP. Les cabinets de consultations se trouvent dans les cantons de Genève, Vaud, Fribourg, Neuchâtel et Jura.
## Description du poste ##
Au sein de l-Unité de médecine et psychologie du trafic (UMPT), vous participez, sous supervision, aux expertises d-aptitude à la conduite automobile réalisées sur les différents sites de l-unité. Pour ce faire, vous collaborez étroitement avec les psychologues de l-UMPT dans le cadre de l-évaluation des situations qui vous sont confiées et contribuez à une prise en charge interdisciplinaire de qualité.
Dans le cadre de vos activités, vous effectuez également des prélèvements biologiques destinés à des analyses toxicologiques et rédigez des rapports d-expertise qui sont validés et co-signés par le ou la médecin responsable de l-unité.
Afin de développer vos compétences dans ce domaine spécialisé, vous participez à des séminaires scientifiques ainsi qu-à des enseignements de formation prégraduée en médecine du trafic, dispensés en français et/ou en allemand.

Vous êtes titulaire du diplôme de médecin ou disposez d'une formation jugée équivalente par la Commission des professions médicales (MEBEKO).

## 50-100% in Winterthur oder Basel ##
Telemedizin ist keine Zukunftsvision mehr - sie ist Alltag. Und santé24 gehört zu den etablierten Playern in der Schweiz. Mit einem grossen interdisziplinären Angebot im Bereich Prävention, Lifestyle(Change) und Patientenbegleitung ergänzen wir unsere ärztliche Grundversorgung.

Bei santé24, der Onlinepraxis von SWICA stellst Du Diagnosen, behandelst und berätst Versicherte mit echten allgemeinmedizinischen Anliegen: telefonisch, strukturiert, mit klinischer Tiefe. Du arbeitest in planbaren Schichten und weisst immer, wann deine Schicht verlässlich endet.

Dabei bist du eingebettet in ein interdisziplinäres Team verschiedener Gesundheitsfachpersonen und in ein interdisziplinäres Ärzteteam - ohne eigenes Praxisrisiko, ohne Patientenadministration auf eigene Rechnung.
### So gestaltest du Gesundheit mit ###
* Telefonische Konsultationen: Diagnose, Therapie, Triage - nach internen Leitlinien
* Rezepte, AUF-Zeugnisse, Physiotherapieverordnungen, Laboranordnungen
* Digitale Dokumentation im Patienteninformationssystem (immer auf Deutsch)
* Interdisziplinäre Zusammenarbeit mit internen Fachpersonen aus Pflege, Pharmazie, Psychologie, Ernährungsberatung, Bewegungscoaching, Physiotherapie u.a.
* Schichtbetrieb: 4-, 6- oder 8-Stunden-Schichten, auch an Wochenenden
* Ca. 2 Pflicht-Präsenztage pro Monat am Standort, restliche Tage im Home-Office (nach einer vierwöchigen Einarbeitungszeit vor Ort in Winterthur und/oder Basel)
* Mehr spannende Informationen und ein Video rund um die Tätigkeit als Ärztin/Arzt bei santé24 findest du auf unserer Karriereseite
### Das zeichnet dich aus ###
* Erfahrung in der Allgemein- oder Inneren Medizin
* FMH Allgemeine Innere Medizin bevorzugt - andere Facharzttitel bei hoher allgemeinmedizinischer Beratungssicherheit willkommen (z.B. praktischer Arzt, Orthopädie, Rheumatologie, Gynäkologie, Kinder- und Jugendmedizin, Notfallmedizin, Dermatologie)
* Sicherer Umgang mit und Freude an digitalen Arbeitsmitteln
* Deutsch und Englisch auf C1-Niveau; weitere Landessprache auf C1-Niveau von Vorteil

The Cardiologist will provide comprehensive care for patients who have illnesses within the scope of cardiology. The scope of these activities covers all phases of ambulatory care.

Additional duties include the following: Administrative Writes Medical Orders and prescriptions for non-controlled substances, as necessary, for the care of the patient in accordance with Federal and State law and approval of the supervising Physician. Documents care provided in the Computerized Patient Record System (CPRS).

Documents the detailed, targeted, initial history and physical examination required for evaluation in the electronic tool(s) required by VA. Obtains consent and documents procedures performed for which the physician is responsible.

Provides education and counseling of patients and families in preventive care, medical conditions, and the use of prescribed treatments and drugs. Reviews and revises policies and scope of practice/standards of operation to meet the needs of the National VA and VA Texas Valley Coastal Bend Health Care System mandates.

Reviews and guides protocols in chronic patient managements including coordinating efforts with fee facilities to meet patients needs and maintain fiscal responsibility.

Clinical Responds to and completes consults received for the evaluation of Cardiology including: Performs a comprehensive, detailed, targeted, initial history and physical examination in compliance with national guidelines. Orders diagnostic studies such as laboratory tests, X-rays, electromyography (EMG), electrocardiograms (EKGs) and other tests.

Consults other disciplines, as necessary, to complete the patient evaluation. Carries out health promotion and disease prevention activities including education and shared decision-making.

Competence in cardiology procedures is desirable and documentation of procedures within the past 12 months will be requested reflective of the scope of privileges requested. Participate in all VISN and national level efforts in cardiac programs Responsible for all aspects of Cardiology care.

Provide or assist residents and/or the nurse practitioner in the process of evaluation and treatment of the cardiology patients, and actively participate in corrective actions against untoward responses to cardiac interventions. Evaluate the patient to assess changes in the physical and mental status.

A progress note is written in the patient's chart. Notes also include the concurrence with notes written by the resident, and attending notes as appropriate. Perform outpatient cardiology consultation reviews, evaluations and treatment.

Participate in various committees, departmental and hospital in-service programs, and education programs; Involved in continuous quality improvement through peer review process. Staff cardiologists shall be responsible for outpatient care, and graduate and undergraduate medical education, and scientific research as appropriate.

Currently employed physician(s) in VA who met the requirements for appointment under the previous qualification standard at the time of their initial appointment are deemed to have met the basic requirements of the occupation.

Basic Requirements: United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy. Degree of doctor of medicine or an equivalent degree resulting from a course of education in allopathic medicine or osteopathic medicine.

Residency Training: Physicians must have completed residency training, approved by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs in an accredited core specialty training program leading to eligibility for board certification.

Exceptions: Residents currently enrolled in ACGME/AOA accredited residency training programs and who would otherwise meet the basic requirements for appointment are eligible to be appointed as "Physician Resident Providers" (PRPs).

PRPs must be fully licensed physicians (i.e., not a training license) and may only be appointed on an intermittent basis. PRPs are not considered independent practitioners and will not be privileged; rather, they are to have a "scope of practice" that allows them to perform certain restricted duties under supervision.

Additionally, surgery residents in gap years may also be appointed as PRPs.

A full-time position is available for Medical Director of the Substance Use Disorders Team (Gold Team) in the VA North Texas Health Care System, Mental Health Service (VANTHCS MHS) in Dallas, Texas.

Core responsibilities include leading and coordinating the operations of a multidisciplinary outpatient mental health team with a focus on uninterrupted high-quality care to Veterans. Incumbent monitors and ensures compliance with hospital and mental health policies, regulations, executive orders and management directives.

Incumbent will collaborate with other teams/team leaders to improve communication and to ensure ongoing continuity of care for Veterans.VA offers a comprehensive total rewards package. VHA Physician Total Rewards.

Duties include but are not limited to: In conjunction with the Clinical Directors of this Mental Health Team, the incumbent plans, organizes, and directs administrative, operational, patient and personnel activities for the team. Duties include coordinating interdisciplinary staffing, work assignments, resource allocation and direct patient care.

Incumbent should be skilled in providing comprehensive psychiatric medical care (assessment, consultation, treatment) with a focus on providing care to Veterans with addictions and substance use disorders.

Incumbent must be skilled in general outpatient psychiatry and addiction psychiatry, including diagnostic evaluations, pharmacotherapy and psychotherapy.

He/she should be competent in the management of individuals with a broad range of clinical problems, including but not limited to substance use disorders, mood, anxiety and psychotic disorders, post-traumatic stress disorder, and psychiatric disorders in the elderly Veteran population.

Incumbent is encouraged to be involved in medical student, psychiatry resident, and addiction psychiatry fellow education. In addition to administrative supervision, he/she may provide clinical supervision and act as collaborating physician for health care professionals such as Nurse Practitioners and Physician Assistants.

Veterans served by the Gold Team tend to have serious and severe crises, be dually diagnosed, and have numerous psychosocial deficits. Treatment provided occurs through an outpatient clinic in Dallas (main campus), an outpatient opioid replacement program, and an Intensive Outpatient Program (IOP).

VANTHCS MHS provides a full range of mental health services including general adult psychiatry, geriatrics, forensics, psychosomatic medicine, substance abuse sub-specialty services, trauma services, psychosocial rehabilitation and recovery programs, comprehensive homeless programs, peer support services, opiate replacement programs, Mental Health Intensive Case Management, vocational rehabilitation programs, domiciliary based programs and inpatient programs.

There is ongoing active research in addiction psychiatry, post-traumatic stress disorder, disaster psychiatry, mood disorders, and homelessness.
